_why: D-158: the CITE runs are the strongest external evidence this project has, and until
this file existed they were re-earned by somebody remembering. This is what a nightly
FAILURES ONLY, and that is deliberate. The 2026-08-26 note is explicit that scope is
not comparable between runs -- 420 assertions attempted one day and 395 another, on
unchanged code, because TEAM Engine attempts what the capabilities document lets it.
So a total that moves is not a regression and cite-count.py does not treat it as one.
A failure is: it means an assertion was attempted and the answer was wrong.
Lower a baseline in the same commit that earns it. Raising one is a decision about
what this server claims, and belongs in an ADR rather than in a passing build.

note: The recorded hand run of 2026-08-21 was 405 of 420 with a different scope. What is
comparable between them is the failure count, and both are what they are because
the untested share is large: WFS 2.0's suite skips whole conformance classes when
the capabilities document does not advertise them, and this server advertises the
Simple WFS class.
ADR-042 condition 3 records the run that discharged it: 0 failed, 25 skipped. The
24 untested here are the same shape -- Part 2 assertions this server does not claim.
Six is the number ADR-041 condition 6 recorded when it was discharged by running
it -- 187 passed, 6 failed -- and it is a baseline rather than a target. It is the
only non-zero one here, so it is the only place a regression could hide behind an
existing failure; the count is exact for that reason.
Lowered to five on 2026-09-27: the scheduled run and a dispatched one both failed
five, so one of the six had come right in the weeks the WFS regression was hiding
the whole workflow's red. Which one is in the cite-reports artefact of run
2026-10-04: a public image service joined the fixture for WCS and WMTS and became a
WMS layer, which gave query_layers-not-queryable its first non-queryable layer to
ask about. It failed -- LayerNotDefined where LayerNotQueryable is due -- and was
fixed in the same commit that added the fixture, so the five are the same five.
Lowered from 10: every one asked for OGC's standard dataset by title (cite:Lakes and ten
more), which the fixture did not have and a layer could not be given. ADR-179 gave layers
a title, and the CITE workflow publishes OGC's own dataset for this suite and removes it
after, so the suite's other 57 checks -- which it skipped without the data -- ran too.
Lowered from 9: the GetFeature-by-POST defaults (service and version taken from a 1.1.0
body), ogc:EID in Id_Capabilities, and NAMESPACE are fixed. The four left are the
engine's own: its Schematron for ExceptionReport is broken in the published image
(ets-wfs11 issue #109), so a well-formed report fails it. D-290.
First run 2026-10-04: 5 failed, all fixed with the run -- InvalidAxisLabel and
InvalidSubsetting answered 400 where WCS 2.0.1's exception table gives 404, a second
subset on one axis intersected instead of refused, and a bogus mediaType ignored.
ADR-170 condition 1.
Lowered from 15: SECTIONS, ServiceProvider, an unknown REQUEST as InvalidParameterValue,
GetFeatureInfo as OperationNotSupported 501, and every GetTile refusal Table 28 names
(layer, style, format, set, matrix, row and column) on the image-service WMTS too.
The first run's three failures were the suite's own -- it starts nothing without a
tile matrix set URI, a URL template, a level and a row and column range, which
tools/cite-run.sh now hands it. Nothing on the server changed.
ADR-169 condition 1: WFS 2.0's Transactional class, as an editor, through
tools/cite-proxy.py. Nine are updateGMLName and nine replaceFeature, and all eighteen
are one gap: gml:name and gml:description are read and dropped, because a layer has no
column for them, so reading the feature back does not return them. Storing GML's
standard properties is a schema decision, not a fix. D-290.

ogcapi-maps-1.0.run: 2026-10-06, 13 passed / 4 failed / 7 untested of 24 test methods (local, ETS 83d2560)
note: ADR-175. Not EARL: the suite runs as its own jar (tools/cite-run-maps.sh) and these
count TestNG methods. Three of the four test classes this server does not claim, which
the suite runs regardless -- tilesets-map links, TIFF and CORS. The fourth asks a fully
transparent background to carry bgcolor's RGB, which a premultiplied PNG cannot: at
alpha 0 the channels are 0. The seven untested need void areas, styles or
api-operations, none claimed.

ogcapi-processes-1.0.run: 2026-10-06, 49 passed / 0 failed / 5 untested of 54 attempted (run 37434627197; the run before, 37432299384, failed 1)
note: ADR-174. The failure was the process list ignoring limit (/req/core/pl-limit-response):
?limit=1 answered all eight. The list and the job list now page, with a next link.
The engine is anonymous, so cite.yml shares the geometry service publicly for the run.

wcs10.run: 2026-10-07, 46 passed / 1 failed (run 37581324130; TEAM Engine console, tools/cite-run-wcs10.sh)
note: ADR-173. Not EARL: the console's EARL is empty in -test mode, so cite-count.py reads its
log, one line per test, an inherited failure not counted twice. The first local run was
38 passed, 9 failed; eight were this server's and are fixed. The one left is the suite's
arithmetic: bbox-inside moves each side of the envelope 1 unit inwards, which inverts a
box under 2 units high -- the fixture's coverage is 1.92 degrees -- and expects content.
